questions.stem: The general molecular formula for alkanes is:
questions.explanation: Alkanes — saturated (all single bonds) hydrocarbons — formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Methane (n=1, CH₄), ethane (n=2, C₂H₆), propane (n=3, C₃H₈). Alkenes (one C=C double bond) — CₙH₂ₙ. Alkynes (one C≡C triple bond) — CₙH₂ₙ₋₂. Cycloalkanes — CₙH₂ₙ (same as alkenes but saturated ring).

questions.stem: LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) sold in Indian cylinders is chiefly a mixture of:
questions.explanation: LPG — mostly butane (C₄H₁₀) and propane (C₃H₈), with a small amount of ethane. Both gases liquefy under moderate pressure, which is why they can be stored in cylinders. Ethyl mercaptan (a sulphur compound) is added as an odourant for leak detection. CNG used in vehicles and piped gas — mostly methane. Methane is the main constituent of natural gas.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The first member of the alkyne series — with a triple bond — is:
questions.explanation: The first alkyne is ethyne (C₂H₂, H-C≡C-H) — also called acetylene. Methane-based alkyne isn't possible (need ≥ 2 carbons to form a triple bond). Acetylene burned with oxygen gives a flame temperature of ~3,100 °C — used in oxy-acetylene welding / cutting of steel. It's also the starting material for making PVC (via vinyl chloride) and many other chemicals.

questions.stem: The gas that ripens fruits (commonly used artificially to ripen mangoes and bananas) is:
questions.explanation: Ethylene (ethene, C₂H₄) — a plant hormone naturally produced by ripening fruit. Commercially used in ripening chambers. Calcium carbide (CaC₂) was widely (illegally) used in India — it reacts with moisture to release acetylene (a mimic hormone) + traces of arsenic / phosphorus (harmful); banned under the PFA / FSSAI Rules. Food-grade ethylene sachets or gas rooms are the safer legal alternative.

questions.stem: Two compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements are called:
questions.explanation: Isomers — same molecular formula, different structure. Example — butane (n-butane, straight chain) and isobutane (2-methylpropane, branched) are C₄H₁₀. Isotopes — same element, different neutrons. Allotropes — same element, different physical forms (diamond vs graphite). Homologues — members of a series differing by a -CH₂- unit (methane, ethane, propane …).

questions.stem: Petrol / diesel are obtained from crude oil by:
questions.explanation: Crude oil is a mixture of hundreds of hydrocarbons. In a refinery, it is vaporised and passed up a tall fractionating tower; different fractions condense at different levels by boiling point — petroleum gas (lowest) < petrol < naphtha < kerosene < diesel < lubricating oil < fuel oil < bitumen (residue at the bottom). India's major refineries — Jamnagar, Paradip, Vadinar, Kochi, Mathura, Panipat.

questions.stem: The 'octane number' of a petrol fuel is a measure of its:
questions.explanation: Octane number — how well a petrol resists 'knocking' (pre-ignition by compression, causing engine rattle). Higher number = higher resistance = suits higher-compression engines. Iso-octane is rated 100, heptane 0; a petrol rated 95 behaves like a 95:5 iso-octane:heptane blend under test. Tetraethyl lead was the original anti-knock additive; phased out for health / environmental reasons. Modern alternatives — ethanol, MTBE. India's petrol is mostly 91-95 RON; premium / 'power' grades go to 97-100.
